senses.definition: The sound of laughing, produced by air so expelled; any similar sound.
examples: Their loud laughter betrayed their presence.

quotes.text: There was some laughter, and Roddle was left free to expand his ideas on the periodic visits of cowboys to the town.
quotes.reference: 1899, Stephen Crane, chapter 1, in Twelve O'Clock:

senses.definition: A movement (usually involuntary) of the muscles of the laughing face, particularly of the lips, and of the whole body, with a peculiar expression of the eyes, indicating merriment, satisfaction or derision, and usually attended by a sonorous and interrupted expulsion of air from the lungs.

quotes.text: The act of laughter, which is caused by a sweet contraction of the muscles of the face, and a pleasant agitation of the vocal organs, is not merely, or totally within the jurisdiction of ourselves.
quotes.reference: 1646, Thomas Browne, Pseudodoxia Epidemica: […], London: […] T[homas] H[arper] for Edward Dod, […], →OCLC:

quotes.text: Archly the maiden smiled, and with eyes overrunning with laughter.
quotes.reference: 1858 October 16, Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, “The Courtship of Miles Standish”, in The Courtship of Miles Standish, and Other Poems, Boston, Mass.: Ticknor and Fields, →OCLC:
